name: Enlarged-pupil cosplay lenses

card.summary: Decorative contact lenses printed with oversized pupils or irises, used to give eyes a wide, doll-like or character look for cosplay and photos.
card.note: Non-corrective lenses are regulated as medical devices in the US; poorly fitted lenses can affect vision.

quick.overview:
Enlarged-pupil cosplay lenses are decorative contact lenses whose printed design makes the pupil or dark iris area look larger. They are used to create character looks, a wide-eyed appearance or a doll-like effect.

They belong to the family of cosmetic lenses that includes circle lenses, which tint the outer rim of the iris to make it appear bigger. Effects last only while the lenses are worn.
quick.how: People buy them as cosmetic soft lenses, usually from eye-care providers or licensed sellers, and wear them for photos, events or costumes. A clear central zone keeps vision usable.
quick.risks: In the US the FDA classifies decorative non-corrective lenses as medical devices requiring clearance and a prescription. Wikipedia notes that poorly fitted tinted soft lenses can temporarily reduce vision in bright and dim light, and that concerns center on buying without seeing an optometrist [1].

lead: Enlarged-pupil cosplay lenses are non-corrective cosmetic contacts designed so the eye looks larger or darker. They sit within the broader category of circle or big-eye lenses, which have been sold since about 2004, launching in Korea, and are popular across East, South and Southeast Asia [1].

Circle lenses add a heavily tinted outer rim that makes the iris look wider and strengthens the limbal ring, while a clear center preserves vision; stated sizes such as 16 mm or 18 mm describe the visual effect, not the lens diameter, which is up to about 15 mm [1].

chain: Wide-eyed or character look in person and photos
angle.text: The lens print changes how large the iris or pupil appears while worn. Users choose it for costumes and a wide-eyed look.

paras: Regular tinted lenses color only the iris area; circle-style designs extend color or a dark ring outward [1]. Pupil-enlarging cosplay variants apply the same printing principle to character designs.

In the US the FDA treats decorative non-corrective lenses as medical devices; sale requires clearance and a valid prescription, and uncleared products may be seized by US Customs [1]. Wikipedia cites a meta-analysis finding tinted lenses appear safe when properly prescribed and used correctly [1].
No studies found specific to enlarged-pupil cosplay lenses. A meta-analysis of tinted lenses in general is described on Wikipedia [1].

timeline.event: Circle lenses begin sale, launching in Korea [1].
